CONSTRUCTION SKILLS
7.1
INTRODUCTION
We nave to go through many steps in order to construct a garment. Each step has its own
importance. If any step is left out, the garment can not be constructed properly. Hence
it is essential for a proficient tailor to be well versed in all the various steps, which may
be-seams, darts, tucks pleats, button hole, button, hook and eye, etc. But let us first learn
the meaning of these terms, their types and their uses.
7.2
OBJECTIVES
After reading this lesson you will be able to :
•
explain the various steps in garment construction;
•
explain about their uses in various garments.
7.3
SEAM'S: THEIR MEANING, NEED AND TYPES
MEANING
~ seam is made by joining two or more pieces of fabric together.
(a)
Need for seams
1.
Tojoin the different parts of a garment.
2.
To shape the garment according to the shape ofthe body.

Types of seams
Seams are of the following
types :-
1.
Plain seam
The seam made by laying two pieces of fabric together and stitching
1 em inside
the edge is known
as plain seam. This seam is used on most materials.
Fig 7.1 Plain seam.
2.
Pinkedge seam
When the edges of the fabric are pinked after a plain seam, it is known as pinkedge
seam. This seam ismade
on seam allowances
as in a ladies kameez v:_,in;:; ;-,f r;. :
blouse,
etc. This is done to prevent the edge from fraying.
Fig 7.2 Pink edge seam.
3.
Flat seam
This is also known as the 'run and fell seam'. This kind of seam is generally used
in gents garments like sides of shirts, in pyjamas, etc. To make this seam, one side
is cut slightly larger than the other. The first seam is given along the edge of the
smaller piece. The larger side is then turned in and tacked to cover the first seam.

Top seam

5.
French seam
The first seam is made just inside the edge the fabric, on the right side. The seam
is then turned over and another seam is made on the wrong side but covering the
first seam. In this kind of seam, no raw edge is visible hence there is no fraying.
It is generally
used on synthetic
fabrics and for children's
garments.

Tacking Plain Seam
This seam is used on the back seams of pants and coats. The seam allowance
is
pressed open after a plain seam is made and the raw edge on both sides is turned
under and secured by tacking.
7.
Press Open Seam
When the seam allowance of a plain seam is pressed open with an iron, it is known
as press open seam. It is used on some particular
seams of some garments.

7.4
MEANING, NEED AND TYPES OF DARTS
a)
Meaning of Darts
Darts are used to dispose of fullness in a garments or to mould the garment to the body
and give a good fit. The extra cloth is taken up at the back ofthe garment and stitched
along the line indicated in the pattern.
b)
Need for Darts
1.
To give shape and fullness to a garment.
2.
To make the garment well fitting.
3.
To make the garment decorative and attractive.

72 :: Home Science
c)
Types of Darts
Darts are used in various types of garments. They have a special importance in dress
making. Darts are mainly of two types, which are as follows :-
1.
Single Point Dart.
2.
Double Point Dart.
1.
Single Point Dart
This type of dart is used in blouses, frocks and at the waist of trousers. It is wide at one
end and pointed at the other end. When the cloth is overlapped about 1-2ems and stitched
in a tapering m:annertill it reaches a single point, it is known as single point dart. These
darts are generally used to dispose of fullness at particular places in garments from where
they derive their names.
i)
WaistDart
This dart is used to give fitting at the waist and is used in blouses, frocks, etc.
Fig 7.7 Waist Dart
ii)
SideDart
This dart is used to dispose of fullness at the bust. It isvaried from wide to narrow
according to the bust measurement. A wide side dart is used for a heavy bust and
anarrow dart isused fora slightbust. This kind of dart isused inblouses, housecoats,
etc. [Fig 7.8 (a)]
ill)
Arm HoleDart
This is made like the waist dart and the side dart. It starts from the curve ofthe
ann hole and tapers inside towards the center. [Fig 7.8 (b)]

iv)
Center Dart
/
This is also known as the 'bust dart'. It could be given either straight or diagonally.
In ladies blouse it is given diagonally from the center front line and tapers inside
towards the center.
/
Fig 7.9 Center Dart
v)
Fish Dart
This dart is shaped like a fish. It starts out narrow and then widens slightly and
then tapers out to a point. It is given at the waist of one piece pants and from the
bottom of the armhole to the waist in a coat.
2.
Double Point Darts
Double pointed darts have pointed ends at the top and bottom and are wide at the center.
It is generally used in ladies shirt and in the back of men's shirt.
i)
French Dart
When a double point dart is made in a garment and cut from the center, it is known
as a French dart.

ii)
~Press Open Dart
'
When the dart is pressed flat after being made, it is known as press open dart.
It is generally used in garments made of heavy fabrics.

followingtypes:-

Pin tucks
These tucks are as thin as a pin and hence are called pin tucks. These are made
by machine at even widths. These are used to make garments attractive. Pin tuck
can be made in any direction and get their name according to the shape in which
they are made.

7.6
PLEATS - MEANING, NEED & TYPES
a)
Meaning
When the extra width of material is folded over systematically to dispose of fullness in a
garment it is known as a pleat.
b)
Need
1.
To make a flair in a garment.
2.
To dispose of fullness in a garment.
3.
To give a decorative touch to a garment.
c)
Types of pleats
Pleats are used to generate designs and also to get a good fitting in a garment. Pleats can
be of the following types:-
1.
Straight Pleats
These are simple and one-sided pleats. The extra width kept for pleats is folded
over and decreased to fit the measurement. All the pleats must be facing in the
same direction. One must also remember to keep the width and fold ofthe pleats
even and equal. This kind of pleats are generally used in skirts and frocks. (Fig
7.12 (a)]

2.
Box Pleats
The fabric is folded on the right side and stitched length wise for about 2-4 inches
from the edge. The broad pleat is then pressed flat by bringing the crease of the
fold over the seam. The two equal pleats obtained on either side of the seam are
known as box pleats. These are generally used in men's garments.
[Fig 7.16 (b)]
3.
Inverted Pleat
When a box pleat is made on the wrong side of the fabric it is known as inverted
pleat [Fig 7.17 (a)]

Knife Pleat

6.
False Pleat
When a pleat is made in order to conceal defects in garment construction, it is
known as a false pleat.

7.7
BUTTONHOLE
Some garments have an opening or aplacket for ease of wearing or removing the garment.
Button holes are made to close the placket. Button holes are mainly of two types:-
i)
Worked button hole
it)
Bound button hole.
1.
Worked button hole
This is also known as the plain button hole. It can be made both'by machine and by hand.
, When making by machine, the button hole stitch is'worked on both sides of the line marked
for the button hole and the slit is made after completing the button hole. When making by
hand, the button hole stitch is worked round the slit for the button hole. Worked button
holes are made in various shapes, such as -

i)
The fan shaped button hole is round at one end and is bound at the other. The
rounded end is called the fan. An even tension must be kept while working this
kind of button hole. [Fig}.18 (i)]
it)
Some button holes are rounded at both ends. These are generally made where
thick buttons are to be used. These are also made in delicate fabrics. [Fig 7.18
(ii)]
iii)
Some button holes have a square end on both sides, There are generally used in
men's and children's garments [Fig 7.18 (iii)]

Tailor button hole.is shaped like a flame. It has a
flame shaped end and the other side is square. It
is generallymade 1-2point, largerthan the button.
To work this kind of button hole, a thick thread
is kept along the edge while the button hole stitch
is being worked.
Fig 7.19 Tailor button hole
Button holes are made in different sizes according to the garments. They are made
according to the size of buttons to be used. Button holes are generally of 5 pt. in
shirts and 6 pt. in pants.
2.
Bound button hole
To make this kind ofbutton hole, a piece of fabric is placed over the mark for
the button hole and then turned inwards to bind the edges. Hence it is called the
bound button hole. It is oftwo types -
i)
Single bound
it)
Double bound
A piece offabric is placed over.the mark for the button hole and stitched in place.
The fabric is then trimmed leaving a 1em margin beyond the seam. The slit for
the button hole is then made and the extra cloth is then neatly turned inwards and
hemmed into place. It is generally used in ladies coat.

7.8
BUTTONS
After making the button holes, buttons are stitched for closing the placket in the garment.
The size ofthe buttons and the button holes should be matching. Buttons can be of the
following kinds :-
~
Simple/shirt button
ii)
Fancy button
ill)
Linen button
iv)
Press button
v)
Coat button
vi)
Pant button
i)
Simple buttons
These are pear buttons with two or four holes. The thread used for fastening is
visible over the button. These buttons get their names according to the garments
they are used on such as - kurta button,
pant button, shirt button, etc. After
sewing on the button the thread is wound round, under the button and then fastened
off on the wrong side. Buttons are available in all colors but nowadays transparent
buttons are also available which can conveniently be used on garments of any
colour.
ii)
Fancy buttons
These buttons are available in many sizes and shapes. They are made of plastic

(pearl), glass, shell, wood or metal. Glass buttons sometimes have designs on
them. The shapes vary from round to square or triangular. Fancy buttons could
be used as fasteners or simply as decorative buttons on the garment.

Linen buttons

7.9
HOOKANDEYE
- ..
These are also used to close placket openings in various garments. Hooks are ofn.vo
types. They are named according to the garments they are used ~n, like pant hook, blouse
hook, press hook, etc. Hooks and eyes are ofthe following types.
1.
Blouse hook
These are also known as 'small hooks' because they are small in size. These are
made of steel or brass. These are used on frocks and saree blouses. The hook
is always stitched on the overlapping side. The hook is paced at the marked place
and stitched on three sides by using the buttonhole stitch.
The eye is made on the other side of the placket. It is usually 2 points long. It is
made by taking a tacking stitch two or three times at the same place and then
binding the stitch by the button hole stitch. A metallic eye may also be used' and
it is stitched on in the same manner as the hook.
-

2.
Pant hook
These hooks are larger in size and are used.in pants, knickers, etc. These hooks
are used with a metallic eye. The hook and eye are fixed at the waistband and
are stitched on by using the buttonhole stitch.

3.
Press hook
Press hooks and eyes are fixed on the garment by piercing the cloth and then
pressing them in place. The advantage of using these hooks is that they take less
time to fix and there is no need for needle and thread. Most tailors prefer to use
these hooks nowadays.
7.10
PRESS BUTTONS
These are commonly used fasteners. Since these are pressed closed, they are called press
buttons. Press buttons have two parts - the thicker part is stitched on the lower end of
the placket and the thinner one is stitched on the overlapping side of the placket. Both are
stitched on with the help ofthe button hole stitch. Both the parts have four holes which
are used for stitching them on the garment. These buttons are available in 2-3 sizes and
are used in children's garments.
Fig 7.24 i) Ring ji) Socket Hi) Bottom
7.11 WHAT YOU HAVE LEARNT
In this lesson you have learnt about various kinds of seams, tucks, pleats, darts, their
names and their uses. You have also learnt about button holes, buttons, hook and eye and
press buttons and how all these can be used for closing openings in garments and their
use in giving the garment a good fitting and a decorative touch.
